exposure: Fetal Pillow use during second-stage cesarean section
conventional disimpaction methods during second-stage cesarean section (vaginal disimpaction, abdominal disimpaction, breech extraction, wound extension, tocolytics)
cohort: The study included 100 second-stage cesarean sections performed at Queen Elizabeth The Queen Mother Hospital and William Harvey Hospital between March 2022 and June 2024.
finding: The use of the Fetal Pillow in second-stage cesarean sections did not result in statistically significant differences in most fetal or maternal outcomes compared to conventional methods, but was associated with a significant increase in fetal injuries such as facial bruises.
mod_finding: The Fetal Pillow did not significantly alter most maternal or fetal outcomes compared to conventional methods during second-stage cesarean sections, but was linked to increased fetal injuries, particularly facial bruises.
